gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: The gallery is open daily ___ Mondays, when it closes for cleaning.
gaps.explanation: 'Except' excludes; 'accept' is the verb for receiving willingly.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
The bank agreed to ___ him the money.
gaps.hint: meaning: give temporarily (from the giver's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Lend' means to give something to someone temporarily; the bank lends money. A base verb is needed after 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The new tax law will ___ every small business in the region.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb (to influence); 'effect' is normally the noun.

gaps.sentence: The medicine had an immediate ___ on her pain.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'an immediate'
gaps.explanation: 'Effect' is the noun meaning result; the fixed phrase is 'have an effect on something'.

gaps.sentence: They managed to ___ the champions in the final.
gaps.explanation: 'Beat' takes the opponent as object (beat the champions); 'win' takes the game or prize.
